title: st.data_editor : FutureWarning during insert
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi, I have a data_editor configured to allow inserts (with `num_rows` set to `dynamic` or `add`).
When I try to insert a new row, I get the following warning in my terminal (where I launched my Streamlit app):

```shell
.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/streamlit/elements/widgets/data_editor.py:342: FutureWarning: The behavior of DataFrame concatenation with empty or all-NA entries is deprecated. In a future version, this will no longer exclude empty or all-NA columns when determining the result dtypes. To retain the old behavior, exclude the relevant entries before the concat operation.
  df.loc[row_label] = dict(zip(df.columns, row_values, strict=True))```

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
st.data_editor(
    data=source_df,
    width="content",
    hide_index=True,
    disabled=[],
    num_rows="dynamic",
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Try to insert a new line
2. Warning is display

### Expected Behavior

Don't receive the warning

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.55.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: MacOS
- Browser: Brave


### Additional Information

_No response_

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-14321)
[USER] Thanks for reporting this issue. This warning is currently expected and can be ignored for now. We will likely attempt to fix this with #13211.

This looks resolved by #13812 (merged 2026-03-23). The `st.data_editor` add/edit path now wraps the row assignment in a `warnings.catch_warnings()` block that suppresses this specific pandas `FutureWarning` (see `lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/data_editor.py`; the inline comment there references this issue). On pandas 3.x the underlying deprecation is gone entirely. The fix shipped under the pandas-3 PR, which is why this issue wasn't auto-closed.

Closing as fixed — please reopen if you still hit it on a recent version. Thanks for the report!
